skill.name: review-agent
skill.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.
skill.summary: Review code changes for concrete, actionable defects without modifying the repository.
skill.author: openai

security_audit.summary: One static finding is confirmed because the skill directs the agent to run read-only Git commands. Seven findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around filenames, labels, and example text.

remediation.issue: The skill passes a selected comparison reference to an external Git command.
remediation.suggestion: Validate comparison references and execute Git with separated arguments to prevent shell interpretation.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes for Actionable Defects
content.value_statement: Code changes can introduce defects that broad summaries or style checks miss. This skill performs a read-only review and reports concrete findings by priority.
actual_capabilities: Reviews uncommitted changes, commits, base-branch differences, or a custom target.
Inspects the complete relevant diff and surrounding code before reporting issues.
Checks tests and call sites to confirm that findings are actionable.
Reports correctness, security, performance, and maintainability regressions.
Orders findings from P0 through P3 and cites focused file locations.
Returns a clear no-findings result when no qualifying defect is found.
limitations: The skill reviews code but does not modify files, create commits, or post comments.
Findings depend on the repository context, tests, and history available to the agent.
The skill does not guarantee detection of every defect or hidden runtime behavior.
Base-branch reviews require a resolvable local branch or configured upstream.

use_cases.title: Check Work Before Commit
use_cases.description: Review local changes for regressions before creating a commit or requesting peer review.

use_cases.title: Assess a Branch Difference
use_cases.description: Compare a feature branch with its merge base and identify defects that would enter the target branch.

use_cases.title: Support Release Validation
use_cases.description: Review a selected commit for release blockers, urgent defects, and material test gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Local Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my uncommitted changes. Report only concrete defects introduced by the diff, ordered by priority.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review commit [commit SHA]. Check surrounding code, tests, and call sites. Cite the smallest relevant changed lines.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused review of one commit.

prompt_templates.title: Review Against a Base Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changes that would merge into [base branch]. Use the merge base and report actionable regressions with priority labels.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before opening or merging a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Targeted Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [target] for security and correctness regressions. Trace affected call paths, verify tests, and explain each demonstrated failure scenario.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a change affects sensitive behavior.

output_examples.input: Review the current uncommitted authentication changes.
output: P1: Preserve token expiry validation in the refresh path. The changed branch accepts expired refresh tokens when cached metadata is missing.
Overall assessment: The authentication change has one urgent correctness and security defect. Add coverage for expired tokens without cached metadata.

output_examples.output: No findings. The reviewed change preserves existing behavior, and the relevant tests cover the modified paths.

output_examples.input: Review the feature branch against its base branch.
output: P2: Restore pagination after filtered results. The new filter resets the cursor but does not request the next page.
Overall assessment: The branch has one user-visible pagination regression. Add a test that combines filtering with multiple result pages.

best_practices: Specify the exact commit, branch, or uncommitted change set to review.
Provide relevant acceptance criteria when intentional behavior changes may resemble regressions.
Keep tests and repository history available so the agent can verify findings.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to fix code or create commits because its workflow is read-only.
Do not request style feedback when no meaningful correctness or maintainability impact exists.
Do not treat the review as a substitute for tests, runtime validation, or human approval.

faq.question: What changes can this skill review?
faq.answer: It can review uncommitted changes, a selected commit, a base-branch difference, or another clearly defined target.

faq.question: Does the skill edit my repository?
faq.answer: No. It is instructed not to modify files, create commits, push branches, or post review comments.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Findings use P0 for critical blockers, P1 for urgent defects, P2 for ordinary defects, and P3 for low-impact issues.

faq.question: Will it report style issues?
faq.answer: It excludes style concerns unless they create a meaningful maintainability problem or obscure the code.

faq.question: What happens when no defects are found?
faq.answer: The skill states that no findings were found and adds a brief assessment of remaining test gaps or risks.

faq.question: Does a clean review prove the change is correct?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on available context and cannot guarantee detection of every defect or runtime condition.
